question: bright orange lattice/star at part and crown in front/back views: scalp or lit roots?
method: combo strands + tt05 params (look7 COLOR + rig1 rig + TT 0.5), geometry-identical variants: (a) visible meshes -> flat green emission, (b) all meshes hidden, (c) OCLX_rim energy 0. Front+back beauty at 1024/64 + ID. Region stats in diag_region_stats.json; crops in diagnose.png.

latticeRegion.definition: pixel bbox from base renders: pixels with lum>0.45 and R-B>0.12 and R>0.4 clustered in the crown band above the brow (front) / around the crown (back). Front cols further gated at >25% orange rows (cols 399-623) and rows (181-269 core); bbox unioned with the full crown band rows 103-269.

verdict: SCALP, not lit roots. Green-scalp render removes the orange entirely (orange 0.52->0.00 front, 0.20->0.00 back; green 0.65/0.81 in its place). Hair-only render also removes it (region falls to background-dark 0.16/0.15: sparse roots over nothing). Rim-off keeps it (0.52/0.18). Front lattice = 52% bare scalp between diverging part roots; back lattice = 60% partial (thin hair over scalp) + 5% bare.
whyTop1Missed: hair-top1 BARE<=2% is measured on crown_top physical strips (top-down projection near the apex). The lattice sits on the part/crown slope seen obliquely in front/back views (front rows 103-269, back rows 155-281); those pixels project outside the crown_top strips. The strips miss this region.
consequence: Fix = cover the scalp in the lattice region (root density in region, scalp albedo under hair matched toward hair colour as production does, root angle/lift, part slit density falloff). Not a light/TT/material-hue fix.
